title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: embedded knowledge files in declarative agents built with the toolkit
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing and agent-blocking controls are supported. It correctly reports the disagreement between the launched roadmap item and Learn's unavailable toolkit route, and keeps unpublished toolkit storage and capability-specific billing details open.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes developers and makers embedding PDF, Word and PowerPoint knowledge into declarative agents built with Teams Toolkit for grounding.
claims.quote: Developers and makers can embed knowledge (pdf, doc/docx, ppt) into their declarative agents built with Teams Toolkit for additional grounding capabilities.

claims.claim: Manifest schema 1.9 documents EmbeddedKnowledge as knowledge files locally in the app package.
claims.quote: Indicates that the declarative agent can use files locally in the app package.

claims.claim: Embedded knowledge files are identified by relative paths.
claims.quote: `file` | String | Required. The file relative path for the embedded file.

claims.claim: The manifest permits at most 10 embedded knowledge files.
claims.quote: `files` | Array of File object | Required. List of objects identifying files that contain knowledge the agent can use for grounding. Maximum size of the array is 10.

claims.claim: Each manifest embedded knowledge file has a maximum size of 1 MB.
claims.quote: Embedded knowledge files have a maximum file size of 1 MB

claims.claim: The manifest allows Word .doc and .docx files.
claims.quote: Word document (.doc, .docx)

claims.claim: The manifest allows PowerPoint .ppt and .pptx files.
claims.quote: PowerPoint presentation (.ppt, .pptx)

claims.claim: The manifest allows Excel .xls and .xlsx files.
claims.quote: Excel workbook (.xls, .xlsx)

claims.claim: The manifest allows plain text .txt files.
claims.quote: Plain text (.txt)

claims.claim: The manifest allows PDF files.
claims.quote: Portable Document Format (.pdf)

claims.claim: A developer chooses to declare EmbeddedKnowledge in the agent manifest.
claims.quote: `capabilities` | Array of Capabilities object | Optional. Contains an array of objects that define capabilities of the declarative agent.

claims.claim: The manifest sensitivity label note says its property and Embedded Files are not enabled yet.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are only applied to the agent, when the agent has Embedded Files. This property is not enabled yet, since Embedded Files are not enabled yet.

claims.claim: Agent Builder is a no-code way to create declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Agent Builder provides a simple interface that you can use to quickly build declarative agents by using natural language.

claims.claim: Agent Builder has a direct file upload route for embedded content.
claims.quote: If you're using Agent Builder to build your agent, you can upload files directly from your device or the cloud to embed the content for your agent to use as knowledge.

claims.claim: Agent Builder file upload limits differ from the manifest's 10 files of 1 MB each.
claims.quote:
Users can upload up to 20 files per agent.
| .doc, .ppt, .xls, .xlsx, .txt | 150 MB |
| .docx, .pptx, and .pdf | 512 MB |

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: Agent Builder uploaded files are stored in tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded containers.
claims.quote: Agent creators can use Agent Builder in Microsoft Copilot to upload files for the agent to use as knowledge. Copilot stores the uploaded files in tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded containers.

claims.claim: Files uploaded through Agent Builder count against tenant OneDrive and SharePoint capacity.
claims.quote: The embedded file content is stored in SharePoint Embedded. These files count against the OneDrive and SharePoint capacity in your tenant.

claims.claim: Unlike locally packaged content, SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge retrieval uses content the user can access.
claims.quote: When you configure your agent to use SharePoint and OneDrive content as knowledge, Copilot searches SharePoint and OneDrive files, folders, or sites that a user has access to for grounding information.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Information Barriers are not supported on embedded files.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Information Barriers (IB) isn't supported on embedded files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Any user who can access the agent can see responses grounded in its embedded file content.
claims.quote: Any user who can access the agent can see responses grounded in the embedded file content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The service applies embedded-content sensitivity labels only to agents created with Agent Builder.
claims.quote:
The service only applies sensitivity labels if:
- You create the agent by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder.
- The agent includes embedded files.

claims.claim: Toolkit-packaged labelled files do not currently receive the documented agent-level embedded-content label.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are only applied to the agent, when the agent has Embedded Files. This property is not enabled yet, since Embedded Files are not enabled yet.

claims.claim: Building and testing agents with Agents Toolkit requires administrator-enabled custom app sideloading.
claims.quote: To build agents with Agents Toolkit and other IDEs, you must have your admin enable the ability to sideload a custom app to your tenant.

claims.claim: Allowing custom app uploads permits users to upload custom packages without submitting them to the Teams app store.
claims.quote: This setting determines if a user can upload a custom app package in the Teams app. Turning it on lets you create or develop a custom app to be used personally or across your organization without having to submit it to the Teams app store.

claims.claim: EmbeddedKnowledge adds grounding content rather than declaring actions.
claims.quote:
`files`: List of objects identifying files that contain knowledge the agent can use for grounding.
`actions`: Optional. A list of 1-10 objects that identify plugins that provide actions accessible to the declarative agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block blocks the selected agent for the whole organisation.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the Copilot package rather than only its embedded knowledge.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.

claims.claim: Custom uploads are configured at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Setup policies > Global (Org-wide default) > Upload custom apps.

Go to Teams apps > Setup policies and select Global (Org-wide default) policy.
Turn on Upload custom apps and select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Set-CsTeamsAppSetupPolicy for completeness but says to create and modify app setup policies in the admin center instead.
claims.quote: The existence of this cmdlet is being documented for completeness, but do not use this cmdlet. We require that all creation and modification of app setup polices (not including the assignment or removal of policies from users) happens in the Microsoft Teams & Skype for Business Admin Center

claims.claim: For Agent Builder embedded-file agents, the All agents inventory can filter to agents that use embedded files as knowledge.
claims.quote: In the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center, you can filter the agent inventory to view only agents that use embedded files as knowledge sources.
